title: Web Development Foundations
description: An original starter course introducing the core building blocks of websites.

lessons.title: Client, server, and HTTP
lessons.content: A browser is a client that requests resources from a server. HTTP defines how requests and responses are exchanged. A URL identifies a resource, while DNS helps translate domain names into IP addresses.

lessons.title: Web page structure
lessons.content: HTML describes content and meaning. Semantic elements such as header, nav, main, article, and footer help browsers, assistive technologies, and search engines understand a page.

lessons.title: CSS basics
lessons.content: CSS rules select elements and apply declarations such as color, spacing, borders, and typography. The box model consists of content, padding, border, and margin.

lessons.title: Responsive design
lessons.content: Responsive layouts adapt to different screen sizes. Use flexible widths, CSS Grid or Flexbox, and media queries. Test keyboard navigation and readable text as well as visual layout.

lessons.title: Variables and functions
lessons.content: Use const for values that are not reassigned and let for values that are. Functions package reusable logic and can accept parameters and return results.

lessons.title: DOM and events
lessons.content: The Document Object Model represents a page as objects. JavaScript can select elements, update text, and respond to events such as clicks or form submissions.

title: Python Programming Basics
description: An original introduction to Python syntax, control flow, collections, and functions.

lessons.title: Values and variables
lessons.content: Python variables refer to objects. Common built-in types include int, float, str, and bool. Use meaningful names and keep indentation consistent.

lessons.title: Input and output
lessons.content: print() displays output and input() reads text from the user. Convert input explicitly with int() or float() when numeric calculations are required.

lessons.title: Conditions and loops
lessons.content: if/elif/else chooses a path. for loops iterate over items, while loops repeat while a condition is true, and break exits a loop.

lessons.title: Lists and dictionaries
lessons.content: Lists preserve order and allow indexed access. Dictionaries map unique keys to values and are useful for structured lookups.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.content: Define reusable behaviour with def. Parameters receive inputs, return sends a result to the caller, and docstrings explain purpose and usage.

lessons.title: Errors and testing
lessons.content: Read tracebacks from the bottom upward to find the immediate error. Test normal cases, boundary cases, and invalid inputs.

title: Data Analytics Foundations
description: Learn a simple workflow for turning raw data into useful decisions.

lessons.title: Analytics workflow
lessons.content: Start with a decision or question, define metrics, collect relevant data, validate quality, analyse patterns, and communicate findings with limitations.

lessons.title: Data quality
lessons.content: Check missing values, duplicates, inconsistent units, invalid ranges, and outdated records before drawing conclusions.

lessons.title: Rows, columns, and keys
lessons.content: A table stores records in rows and attributes in columns. A primary key uniquely identifies a row; a foreign key links related tables.

lessons.title: Filtering and aggregation
lessons.content: SQL SELECT retrieves columns, WHERE filters rows, GROUP BY aggregates categories, and ORDER BY sorts the output.

lessons.title: Choosing charts
lessons.content: Use bar charts for category comparisons, line charts for trends over time, and scatter plots for relationships between numeric variables.

lessons.title: Responsible interpretation
lessons.content: Correlation alone does not establish causation. Explain the population, time period, assumptions, and uncertainty behind a result.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning
description: An original overview of supervised learning, evaluation, and responsible model use.

lessons.title: What is machine learning?
lessons.content: Machine learning uses data to fit a model that makes predictions or identifies patterns. It is useful when rules are difficult to specify manually.

lessons.title: Supervised and unsupervised learning
lessons.content: Supervised learning uses labelled examples. Unsupervised learning explores structure in data without a target label, such as grouping similar records.

lessons.title: Train, validation, and test sets
lessons.content: Training data fits model parameters. Validation data helps select settings. A held-out test set estimates performance on unseen examples.

lessons.title: Classification metrics
lessons.content: Accuracy is the fraction of correct predictions. Precision measures how many predicted positives are true positives; recall measures how many actual positives were found.

lessons.title: Overfitting and leakage
lessons.content: Overfitting occurs when a model learns training-specific noise. Data leakage occurs when training uses information unavailable at prediction time.

lessons.title: Responsible AI
lessons.content: Assess data representativeness, privacy, fairness, explainability, and the consequences of mistakes. Monitor models after deployment because data can change.

title: Cloud Computing Fundamentals
description: Understand cloud service models, deployment, access control, and cost awareness.

lessons.title: What is cloud computing?
lessons.content: Cloud computing provides on-demand access to computing resources over a network. Capacity can often be provisioned and released without buying physical servers.

lessons.title: Service models
lessons.content: IaaS provides configurable infrastructure, PaaS provides a managed application platform, and SaaS provides a finished application to end users.

lessons.title: Identity and access management
lessons.content: Grant each identity only the permissions required for its task. Use multifactor authentication where available and remove access when it is no longer needed.

lessons.title: Shared responsibility
lessons.content: Cloud providers secure parts of the underlying service, while customers remain responsible for configured identities, data, applications, and other controls according to the service model.

lessons.title: Availability and backups
lessons.content: Use backups, recovery tests, monitoring, and suitable redundancy to reduce the impact of failures. A backup is useful only if restoration works.

lessons.title: Cost management
lessons.content: Tag resources, set budgets and alerts, right-size instances, and shut down unused development resources. Understand data transfer and storage costs.

title: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
description: Learn defensive security principles, phishing awareness, authentication, and incident response.

lessons.title: Confidentiality, integrity, availability
lessons.content: Confidentiality limits unauthorised disclosure, integrity protects correctness, and availability ensures authorised users can access systems when needed.

lessons.title: Threats and vulnerabilities
lessons.content: A threat may exploit a vulnerability to cause harm. Risk depends on likelihood and impact, and controls can reduce but rarely eliminate risk.

lessons.title: Authentication
lessons.content: Use unique passwords stored in a reputable password manager and enable multifactor authentication. Never share one-time codes or recovery codes.

lessons.title: Phishing awareness
lessons.content: Check the sender, domain, urgency, unexpected attachments, and requests for credentials or payments. Verify sensitive requests using a separate trusted channel.

lessons.title: Updates and backups
lessons.content: Apply security updates promptly, use supported software, restrict permissions, and maintain protected backups.

lessons.title: Incident response
lessons.content: Report suspected incidents quickly, preserve relevant evidence, follow the organisation's response plan, and avoid making changes that destroy useful evidence.

title: Digital Marketing Foundations
description: An original introduction to audience research, SEO, social media, and campaign measurement.

lessons.title: Define the audience
lessons.content: Describe the audience's needs, context, problems, and preferred channels. Build a clear value proposition instead of trying to appeal to everyone.

lessons.title: Set measurable objectives
lessons.content: Use specific goals and a time period. Choose metrics that connect to outcomes, such as qualified leads, conversions, retention, or revenue.

lessons.title: Content planning
lessons.content: Create useful content for a defined audience. Match format and detail to the audience's intent and maintain a consistent publishing workflow.

lessons.title: SEO basics
lessons.content: Use descriptive page titles, helpful headings, accessible content, descriptive links, and fast mobile-friendly pages. Avoid keyword stuffing and misleading claims.

lessons.title: Social media planning
lessons.content: Select channels based on audience behaviour and the content format. Use a calendar, clear calls to action, and a consistent brand voice.

lessons.title: Analytics and experiments
lessons.content: Track relevant metrics, define a baseline, and test one meaningful change at a time when practical. Do not interpret likes alone as business success.

title: Content Creation and SEO
description: Plan accessible content, structure pages, research search intent, and measure performance.

lessons.title: Write a useful brief
lessons.content: A brief states the audience, problem, goal, key message, format, evidence required, call to action, and success metric.

lessons.title: Editorial workflow
lessons.content: Plan research, drafting, fact-checking, accessibility review, approval, publishing, and later updates.

lessons.title: Search intent
lessons.content: Search intent may be informational, navigational, commercial, or transactional. Create a page that genuinely satisfies the likely need.

lessons.title: Page structure
lessons.content: Use a clear title, descriptive headings, meaningful link text, alt text for informative images, and concise metadata. Avoid promising results the page cannot deliver.

lessons.title: Performance measures
lessons.content: Impressions, clicks, click-through rate, conversions, and engagement answer different questions. Interpret them together with the page's purpose.

lessons.title: Content maintenance
lessons.content: Update outdated facts, broken links, examples, and screenshots. Remove or consolidate pages that are duplicative or no longer useful.

title: Business and Project Management Basics
description: Learn objectives, scope, stakeholders, risks, milestones, and team communication.

lessons.title: Project goals and scope
lessons.content: A project has a defined objective, boundaries, deliverables, and constraints. Clear scope reduces confusion about what is included and excluded.

lessons.title: Stakeholders
lessons.content: Identify people affected by or able to influence the project. Clarify their needs, decision rights, communication preferences, and approval responsibilities.

lessons.title: Milestones and dependencies
lessons.content: Break work into manageable tasks, estimate effort, identify dependencies, and set milestones. Revisit estimates when evidence changes.

lessons.title: Risk management
lessons.content: Record each meaningful risk, its likelihood and impact, an owner, a mitigation plan, and a trigger for escalation.

lessons.title: Status reporting
lessons.content: A useful status report covers progress, next steps, blockers, decisions needed, and changes to timeline or scope.

lessons.title: Retrospectives
lessons.content: Review what worked, what did not, and what to change. Assign an owner and due date to each improvement action.

title: Personal Finance and Budgeting Basics
description: An educational introduction to budgeting, saving, interest, risk, and financial decision-making.

lessons.title: Income and expenses
lessons.content: Record income and spending over a consistent period. Separate fixed expenses, variable expenses, needs, wants, and irregular costs.

lessons.title: Emergency savings
lessons.content: An emergency reserve can help cover unexpected essential expenses. A suitable target depends on income stability, obligations, and personal circumstances.

lessons.title: Simple and compound interest
lessons.content: Simple interest is calculated on the original principal. Compound interest earns interest on principal plus previously accumulated interest.

lessons.title: Borrowing responsibly
lessons.content: Compare the total repayment amount, interest rate, fees, tenure, penalties, and affordability. Understand the terms before signing a loan agreement.

lessons.title: Diversification
lessons.content: Diversification spreads exposure across assets or holdings, but it does not eliminate all investment risk or guarantee returns.

lessons.title: Avoiding scams
lessons.content: Be cautious of guaranteed high returns, pressure to act immediately, unclear fees, and requests for OTPs or credentials. Verify providers independently.

title: Healthcare and Biotechnology Introduction
description: An introductory overview of cells, biotechnology, evidence, and healthcare data privacy.

lessons.title: Cells and DNA
lessons.content: Cells are fundamental units of life. DNA stores genetic information, and genes are regions of DNA that contribute to biological functions through products such as RNA and proteins.

lessons.title: Biotechnology
lessons.content: Biotechnology uses organisms, cells, or biological systems to develop products and processes, including diagnostics, medicines, agriculture, and research tools.

lessons.title: Scientific evidence
lessons.content: A scientific claim should be evaluated using the quality of the evidence, study design, sample, uncertainty, and independent replication where appropriate.

lessons.title: Quality and traceability
lessons.content: In regulated settings, records, validated procedures, documentation, and traceability help teams investigate errors and maintain consistent processes.

lessons.title: Privacy and confidentiality
lessons.content: Health data can be highly sensitive. Collect only what is necessary, restrict access, use secure storage, and follow applicable privacy and institutional rules.

lessons.title: Digital health systems
lessons.content: Electronic records and analytics can support workflows, but data quality, access controls, interoperability, and human oversight remain important.

title: Healthcare Operations and Analytics Basics
description: Understand patient-flow concepts, operational metrics, process improvement, and responsible data use.

lessons.title: Patient flow
lessons.content: Patient flow describes movement through services such as registration, assessment, treatment, and discharge. Delays may occur when capacity and demand are mismatched.

lessons.title: Process mapping
lessons.content: A process map makes steps, handoffs, queues, and decision points visible. Teams can use it to locate bottlenecks before proposing changes.

lessons.title: Wait time and throughput
lessons.content: Wait time measures delay before a service step. Throughput measures completed cases over a period. Both need clear definitions and time windows.

lessons.title: Balancing measures
lessons.content: Improving speed should not undermine safety, quality, equity, or staff workload. Evaluate multiple measures rather than optimising one number alone.

lessons.title: Small improvement cycles
lessons.content: Define the problem, establish a baseline, test a small change, measure outcomes, and decide whether to adapt, adopt, or abandon the change.

lessons.title: Ethical data use
lessons.content: Use appropriate permissions, minimise identifiable data, document definitions, and interpret results in context. Operational data should not be treated as a substitute for clinical judgement.
